designDirection: User-supplied low, broad, angular capital ship; layered hull and two paired engine blocks.

prompts.step: Generate five-view Titan sheet from the two user shape references
prompts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: 2D five-view spaceship modeling reference for the TITAN flagship.

The user has now supplied TWO photographs/screenshots showing the silhouette they want. Use THESE TWO images as the primary shape and construction references. Translate the spacecraft proportions and structural character into a new Titan reference sheet. Do not substitute a generic triangular star destroyer, a hammerhead, or a three-pronged ship.

Image 1: primary rear-above shape reference. Study its broad flat armored deck, low profile, chamfered stepped perimeter, long inset side structures, broad rear shoulders, and two massive rectangular stern engine blocks. Each engine block holds a PAIR of tall vertically elongated exhaust apertures.
Image 2: supporting underside/front-quarter shape reference. Study its blunt stepped prow, layered thick central underside, recessed machinery and lateral structural layering. Use it to make the side and bottom coherent with image 1.
The planets, starfields, exhaust trails, camera perspectives and photographic lighting are not part of the desired sheet.

SHAPE DIRECTION:
One low, broad, connected armored capital-ship body. A substantial central slab-like hull with a flattened elongated polygonal planform, a blunt squared-off/chamfered forward end, shallow stepped cut-ins along the perimeter, and layered lateral armor shelves. Long straight raised side spars run along the edges as integrated structural members, not detached forward heads. The bow narrows only moderately into a short blunt prow; no long triangular taper or needle nose. The broad aft shoulders terminate in TWO chunky engine blocks, left and right, attached directly to the main hull, separated by a shallow central stern recess. Keep the heavy aft mass and thin, angular upper deck evident in the references. The underside has a deeper central armored keel and inset machinery, so the side view has convincing layered thickness. Avoid a tall command tower: a low, compact command blister and tiny inset bridge windows fit the deck. Small recessed weapon mounts, armored dorsal weapon blisters, fine panel joins, service hatches, vents and narrow hangar openings communicate capital-ship scale. No gigantic ornamental gun turrets or exposed skyscraper bridges.

ENGINE SIGNATURE:
Exactly FOUR vertically elongated rounded-rectangle / oval exhaust apertures total, arranged in two side-by-side PAIRS: two in the port engine block and two in the starboard engine block. All FOUR point straight backward at the same stern plane; all are tall narrow apertures, not round circles. Cyan-blue luminous cores instead of the orange cores in the photographs, with deep dark rims and a few visible internal nozzle vanes. The two engine blocks remain wide and boxy, with integrated armored roof caps. No extra central engine, no six-engine row, no vertical stack of whole engine blocks, no detached nacelles.

MATERIAL TRANSLATION:
Retain the Stellar Syndicates fleet's materials: pale titanium and silver-gray large armor surfaces, dark charcoal gunmetal inset structure, restrained warm brass hardware/edge accents, small cyan service lights and bridge glazing. Let dark structure and medium-gray secondary plates remain substantial, rather than an all-white featureless hull. Detailed practical industrial construction, subtle wear, crisp panel seams. Make the ship visually imposing and purposeful. This is a new game-art interpretation of the supplied SHAPE, not a change to the shape merely to fit older Titan concepts.

SHEET:
ONE high-resolution wide landscape image, approximately 2:1, warm-white background, precise fully colored hard-surface concept drafting. Exactly FIVE complete, consistent views of this SAME Titan. TOP and BOTTOM occupy the left half as two large plan drawings, both noses pointing UP, same length and beam. FRONT upper right, BACK middle right, SIDE across lower right pointing LEFT. Each drawing must be separate, fully framed with generous spacing. Match lengths between plan and side, and widths between plan and end elevations. Title "TITAN"; labels "TOP", "BOTTOM", "FRONT", "BACK", "SIDE" only. Simple clear typography. No extra explanatory text, comparison ship, perspective hero view, grids across the artwork, dimension arrows, or extra inset drawings.

VIEW CONSISTENCY:
TOP is straight overhead orthographic with zero perspective. Show the exact broad low slab hull, stepped side shelves, blunt prow, integrated long side spars, deck blisters and two aft engine-block roofs. Rear-facing oval apertures must not rotate upward toward this camera.
BOTTOM is straight underneath, nose UP, with precisely the same silhouette, major stepped hull edges, stern recess and two engine-block positions. Fully finished distinct underside: deep protected center keel, dark recessed machinery pockets, plated service corridors, radiators, hangar/docking recesses, small cyan markers and detailed armor continuing to all edges. No copied command windows or dorsal gun blisters on the belly. No blank gray underside. No landing legs.
FRONT is exact level head-on orthographic, zero camera elevation: the forward length collapses. Show one broad low faceted bow cross-section, shallow central bow recess and armored side ledges, with tiny visible deck structures behind. Not an overhead view compressed vertically. No stern engine apertures visible through the bow. No projecting spear sticking up.
BACK is exact level stern-on orthographic. Show the two large rectangular engine blocks and their FOUR tall cyan rounded-rectangle/oval openings: TWO openings per block, side by side. Central stern recess between the blocks, layered rear deck above and belly below. Same total beam and thickness as FRONT. Any dorsal gun barrels point away from this observer; show rear housings, not backwards-pointing muzzle holes.
SIDE is genuine level orthographic with blunt prow LEFT, engine blocks RIGHT. Low armored deck, straight long structural rail, stepped lateral armor, recessed hangar/machinery spaces and the deeper central keel. Engine block is one deep rectangular stern housing with a vertical aperture visible only as a thin rear edge; the far engine block occludes behind the near one. No two engine blocks stacked vertically. Low command blister and gun mounts match TOP.

Avoid returning to any earlier Titan design: no three heads, no separate long forward arms, no pointed triangular wedge, no transverse hammerhead on a narrow neck, no generic naval battleship tower. Preserve the recognizable low, broad, layered gunship/capital-ship shape in the user's two references.
